historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly treats the operation as persistent, but its command omits even the source's interface selector and cannot identify the MAC that would be programmed.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Adds strong identity, uniqueness, persistence and recovery controls; the underlying contract must also resolve whether 0x30/0x40 accepts MAC bytes or copies a pre-existing value.
historical_reviews.history: The invalidated earlier-run artifact was located but excluded as authority; LAN read-back can corroborate active identity but cannot by itself establish EEPROM persistence or field integrity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Persistent network identity mutation requires exact target/source semantics and an independent recovery path before any write.

original_test_intent: Program the approved permanent MAC identity for one selected BMC Ethernet interface into the correct EEPROM field, validate active and persistent identity without collision, and restore the original bytes when the test plan requires rollback.
original_method: Preserve both source request forms and the eth0/eth1 selector definition; issue neither until the Wistron contract resolves request framing, MAC-source semantics, activation behavior and EEPROM mapping.
manual_activity: The network/asset owner identifies the physical interface and EEPROM slot, allocates a globally valid non-conflicting MAC, approves the exact source/payload semantics, activation or reload behavior, and an independent recovery channel with original-image restoration.
required_inputs: Verified BMC/SUT, board and firmware identity
Ruling on selector-required versus no-data request
Definition of whether the command copies current LAN MAC or accepts explicit address bytes
eth0/eth1 to physical port and EEPROM-field map
Complete original EEPROM/MAC baseline and hash
Approved MAC allocation, byte order and validity policy
Activation/persistence timing and any reload requirement
Exact original-MAC restore path and explicit owner approval
safety_requirements: Never guess selector, MAC source, EEPROM field or byte order
Reject multicast, broadcast, locally administered when disallowed, all-zero, all-FF and duplicate MAC values
One interface and one approved write only
Preserve all interface identities before mutation
Do not rely on the affected management session for recovery
Do not reset or power-cycle unless separately approved
Verify both active and persistent identity
Restore the original EEPROM identity on failure or planned rollback
agent_execution_scope: Verify board, interface and EEPROM mapping
Capture LAN inventory, current MACs and EEPROM baseline through approved tools
Check the allocated MAC for syntax, policy and network uniqueness
Display the exact request and resulting programmed value for OK
Observe session/network impact and verify active plus persistent identity
Restore original bytes through the independent path when required
Archive raw, LAN, EEPROM and recovery evidence
engineer_actions: Resolve both request framing and MAC-source semantics
Approve allocation, target field, activation and persistence oracle
Approve an independent recovery path and any separate reset/reload

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its bare OOB 0x30/0x40 omits the source's interface selector and supplies no explicit MAC; without proof that the command copies a known current value, the operation's target and written identity are indeterminate.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After the vendor contract is approved, send exactly one 0x30/0x40 request using the contract-defined selector and MAC-source/payload fields, then verify the selected interface's active and persistent identity through independent LAN and EEPROM evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The eth0=0x00/eth1=0x01 selector definition, both transport forms and 10/5 timing are preserved pending resolution; no MAC bytes are invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat MAC programming as a controlled identity migration: complete baseline, allocation/duplicate validation, one byte-defined EEPROM write, independent reconnection, persistence proof and exact restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the programmed identity explicit and replaces command-success plus lan-print acceptance with EEPROM/active-state integrity and recovery evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A runtime MAC visible in lan print does not prove EEPROM persistence; EEPROM bytes alone do not prove the active interface loaded the intended identity without collision.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A wrong selector or field can corrupt another port's identity, while duplicate or invalid MAC programming can sever BMC management and contaminate inventory or network forwarding state.

project_override_considerations: A manufacturing utility may substitute only with documented access to the same EEPROM field and equivalent byte, persistence and restore evidence; a runtime LAN SET is not equivalent.
expected_evidence: Approved board/interface/EEPROM map, request contract, MAC allocation and owner confirmation
Complete original MAC/EEPROM/LAN inventory and hashes
Exact redacted request bytes, programmed identity, completion and timing
Active-interface MAC, switch/neighbor uniqueness and management-session continuity
Original-MAC restoration and recovered management identity when required

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: For the same 0x30/0x40 operation the in-band Procedure requires an Ethernet Interface Select byte, the OOB Procedure supplies no data, and neither form states the MAC source or payload despite the title claiming an EEPROM MAC write. The vendor contract must resolve these incompatible/incomplete request semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The persistent interface-identity purpose is identifiable. Exact vendor semantics, allocation, target map and recovery are expected package/owner inputs, so execution is gated but the review is not irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Exposes the selector/no-data conflict and unknown MAC source, then requires allocation integrity, active-versus-persistent verification and recovery independent of the interface being modified.
independent_technical_reasoning: A command named Write MAC Address may either carry new address bytes or commit a value already staged elsewhere; the source does not say which. That distinction determines both the payload and evidence. Because changing EEPROM identity may disrupt the same network path used by the agent, success cannot be inferred from pre-disruption completion—independent read-back, collision detection and a recovery channel are essential.
